$comment: Known answers for carpet area vs super built-up area (loading) and the effective price per sq ft of carpet. Published worked examples found via web search on 2026-10-09 (direct fetch of the pages is blocked in the build environment). Loading is quoted two ways in India: on carpet area, (SBA − carpet) ÷ carpet, and as the common share of SBA, (SBA − carpet) ÷ SBA; every case states which figure it gives.

cases.name: 1,300 sq ft super built-up, 1,000 sq ft carpet: 30% loading on carpet
cases.quote: If the carpet area of an apartment is 1,000 square foot (sqft) and the super built-up area is 1,300 sqft, the loading factor = {(1,300−1,000)/1,000} × 100 = 30%

cases.name: 1,500 sq ft super built-up, 1,200 sq ft carpet: 20% of SBA is common area
cases.quote: Loading factor = 1 − (carpet area ÷ super built-up area): 1,500 sq ft super built-up and 1,200 sq ft carpet gives 20%

cases.name: ₹1.80 crore for 1,500 sq ft super built-up with 1,050 sq ft carpet
cases.quote: Advertised area (super built-up) of 1,500 sq. ft. at an apartment price of ₹1.80 crore … ₹12,000 per sq. ft. But if the actual carpet area is only 1,050 sq. ft., the effective cost becomes ₹1.80 crore ÷ 1,050 sq. ft. = ₹17,143 per sq. ft.
